record.title: Instruction-file approval cards render attacker-sized full content with no per-card or aggregate cap, re-rendered on every 2 s poll
record.description: A prompt-injected sandbox agent holding its own agent token can queue PENDING_APPROVALS_MAX=20 pending write_file approvals per sandbox to instruction-file paths (default rule instruction-file-write-needs-approval). Each pending row stores the agent's full 'content', which is exempt from TOOL_ARG_MAX. _approvals.html renders every pending instruction-file card's content in full through autoescape plus _shown (escape_controls turns each non-printable-ASCII character such as U+0001 into a 4-character escape) with no truncation and no aggregate cap. web.render materialises and SHA-256-hashes the whole body on every request, including ones that end in 204, and index.html and sandbox.html both poll the fragment every 2 s; the index fragment aggregates the pending set of all sandboxes. Parent-live evidence against the real API: 20 write_file calls returned 202 (the 21st 429), and each GET /ui/approvals returned 83,920,462 bytes in about 13.7 s. Independent sandboxed reproduction with the real template and filters: 20 x 1 MiB U+0001 cards took 10.85 s to render and hash and produced an 80.0 MiB body, against 0.13 s / 20.0 MiB for printable ASCII. The human approval view becomes unusable while the attacker's writes are pending, and each poll ties up a control-plane worker for seconds of CPU.
record.root_cause: _approvals.html:13 outputs a.args.content in full with no length bound. _shown/escape_controls expands each non-printable-ASCII character about 4x. Neither the card nor the fragment has a rendered-size cap. web.render (web.py:147-148) always builds and hashes the full body before deciding on a 204. Content size is not checked when the approval is created: service.py:359-360 exempts 'content' from TOOL_ARG_MAX, and the max_write_bytes=1 MiB check only runs when the approved write executes (sandbox.py:507). A pending card's content is therefore bounded only by the 8 MiB JSON body limit (config.py:65); the 1 MiB-per-card figure used in the measurements is a conservative lower bound.
record.intended_behavior: The approvals fragment, polled every 2 s from the index and sandbox pages, should cap the CPU and bytes each poll costs, so that pending content chosen by an agent cannot make a poll cost seconds of control-plane CPU or tens of MiB of response, and the human can still review and deny the request.

conditions.description: Attacker holds a per-sandbox agent token (the assumed prompt-injected agent).
A human has an approvals view open; the index and sandbox pages poll /ui/approvals every 2 s automatically.

Up to 20 pending instruction-file write approvals per sandbox, each carrying large content of non-printable-ASCII characters; approvals expire after approval_timeout (default 300 s) and the agent can queue them again.
Default configuration: default_policy.yaml v4, PENDING_APPROVALS_MAX 20, max_body_bytes 8 MiB.

execution.attacker_perspective: As the sandbox agent, fill the per-sandbox pending queue with maximum-size instruction-file writes; every human poll of the approvals view then re-renders them.
payloads: repeat 20 times with different instruction-file paths to reach PENDING_APPROVALS_MAX
instructions: In the sandbox, build a Jinja2 environment for agentbox/templates with autoescape on, finalize=agentbox.web._shown, and filters oneline/short as in web.register.
Construct 20 pending-approval dicts with tool='write_file', preview.instruction_file set, and args.content = '\x01' * (1024*1024).
Render _approvals.html once and record render time and body size.
execution.observed_result: Rendering and hashing 20 x 1 MiB U+0001 cards took 10.846 s and produced an 80.0 MiB body; printable ASCII took 0.131 s for 20.0 MiB. The parent-live run against the real API measured 83,920,462 bytes in about 13.7 s per GET /ui/approvals.

remediation.strategy: In the polled fragment, show only a capped prefix of instruction-file content, with total length, a digest, and a link to a separate non-polled page that shows the full content for the approval under review. Cap the total rendered bytes per fragment. Reject or bound write_file content at max_write_bytes before creating an approval. Base the 204 version on approval ids and statuses, not on a hash of the rendered body.

likelihood.reason: Triggered by a prompt-injected agent under default configuration; the UI polls automatically.

impact.reason: Degrades or denies the human approval UI and ties up control-plane threadpool workers while the human triages the attacker's writes; no data loss or privilege change.

confidence.reason: Measured with the real template and filters in the sandbox and against the real API in a parent-live run; bounds and per-poll rebuild are source-confirmed.
